backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes, without analysts' consensus): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 80% of what happened (11% fell below it, 9% above) — about right. backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 81% of what happened (10% fell below it, 10% above) — about right. Loss-makers' operating margin three years out: inside its 80% range 71% of the time (448 outcomes). The chance of an operating profit within three years scores +0.02 against simply using the share that got there (Brier skill: above 0 is better than that base rate). Cash running out within three years: Brier skill -4.01 against the share that stopped filing (602 loss-makers; stopping includes acquisitions, so it overstates failures).

epv.note: Price above EPV: the market pays for growth. EPV above tangible book: the business earns more than its assets would cost to rebuild — a sign of a moat (Greenwald). EPV below tangible book: the assets earn less than their cost.

implied_return.note: The yearly return a buyer at today's price earns if each model's assumptions hold (an implied cost of capital). Above the cost of equity: the price leaves room; below: the price already asks for more than the models deliver.
